name: Waveshare ESP32-C5-LCD-1.47
summary: The first ESP32-C5 board penguinOS has ever built for: a long thin 320x172 ST7789 strip, no PSRAM, no touch, and a microSD sharing the panel's SPI bus.

render.reason: REWRITTEN FROM ASPIRATION TO WHAT IS ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTED. This block used to say tier 1 / lvgl, and that was a plan, not a description: there is no LVGL anywhere in the tree, EOS_USE_LVGL and EOS_COMPOSITOR_LVGL are read by no translation unit, and the one display backend that exists (kernel/hal/backend/esp_lcd/eos_display_st7789.c) is the banded indexed-8 software compositor with a hardcoded uint16_t lut[EOS_PALETTE_MAX] of 256 entries. So tier 0 / indexed8 / 256 is not a downgrade of this board, it is the first accurate sentence anyone has written about it. band_height is 8, carried over from cyd-4832s040 rather than from the 1.3in and 2.4in boards' 16, because the strips cost 2 x band_height x WIDTH x 2 bytes and WIDTH here is 320: 8 rows is 10,240 bytes against the 15,360 the tightest verified board runs on. Erring small is deliberate - the CYD lesson was that a band height inherited without re-deriving it for a wider panel starves the radio, and the symptom is not a slow screen but a web server that accepts and then drops. MEASURED ON HARDWARE. penguinOS reports 143740 free / 114688 largest at app_main, and 34972 free / 18432 largest once the whole boot sequence has run, in SETUP mode - the worst case, with the SoftAP and the station interface both up. Those are the figures AFTER the Wi-Fi buffer pools were cut in sdkconfig.defaults.esp32c5. Before that cut the same board ended boot with 19592 free and could not hand a phone a DHCP lease: the client associated, waited six seconds without an address and deauthenticated itself. The display is not the expensive thing here and never was - it takes 11944 bytes against the radio's 49108 even after tuning. Do not buy picture quality out of this budget; there is nothing spare in it.

display.pixel_format_reason: RGB565 straight down the wire, two bytes per pixel.
display.clock_reason: 40MHz. This was originally a mirror of the Waveshare BSP's BSP_LCD_SPI_CLK_HZ and explicitly NOT a control. driver_source is now esp_lcd, so it IS a control: eos_display_st7789.c configures the SPI bus at this rate. The value is unchanged because 40MHz is what the vendor clocks this panel at and what the verified S3 board with the same panel runs.
display.byte_swap_reason: MEASURED. Was inherited-not-measured until this board's first light. The setup screen renders amber-on-dark with the QR scanning cleanly, which is the whole test: a wrong byte_swap turns the theme's amber into a blue-green and a wrong invert turns the dark ground light, and both wrong gives yellow. None of those happened.
display.mirror_reason: MEASURED. Both false. Text reads left-to-right and the setup QR scans, which it cannot do mirrored - a QR is not symmetric and a reflected one fails its own format check. Note this DISAGREES with the verified waveshare-s3-touch-lcd-147, which needs mirror_x true for the same 172x320 panel; see the invert-mirror gotcha.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: There is no touch layer and no exposed button on this board, so a BLE keyboard is the only input. NimBLE is the stack penguinOS carries everywhere; keeping one stack across all boards keeps one HID host implementation.

touch.absent_reason: The 1.47in module has no touch layer. The Waveshare BSP capability table lists Touch: No, alongside Buttons: No, Audio: No and IMU: No.

panel_id_register.note: Not attempted, and pointless here anyway: MISO is not wired to the panel, so nothing can be read back from the controller at all.

distinguishing_notes: Long thin 1.47 inch IPS strip, 320x172 in landscape, on a narrow board.
Native USB, so it enumerates as a usb_serial_jtag device rather than a CH340 or CP2102 bridge.
The only C5 board in the fleet with an LCD; the other C5 drives a 128x64 OLED over I2C.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the Waveshare ESP32-C5-LCD-1.47 with the long thin colour strip, and not the C5 wired to the 128x64 mono OLED? Both are ESP32-C5 with 4MB and esptool reports them identically.

gotchas.text: No board in this registry had ever been BUILT for esp32c5 before this one - the other C5 profile (wavvy-oled-c5) has never been flashed either, and there was no firmware/sdkconfig.defaults.esp32c5 at all until this board was brought up. Anything that fails here on the SoC rather than on the panel is a first, not a regression.

This board looks modern and is not roomy. 143740 bytes free at app_main puts it within 4% of the 4.0in CYD, a 2016 ESP32 - but it carries a dual-band Wi-Fi 6 radio whose driver defaults are sized for a part with four times this SRAM. That mismatch is a trap the registry walked straight into: sdkconfig.defaults.esp32 has carried cut-down Wi-Fi buffer pools since the CYD needed them, under a comment saying the trade is NOT to be copied to the other targets because THEY HAVE THE RAM. That was true of every board in the fleet until this one. The C5 shipped with stock pools, spent 62720 bytes on the radio, ended boot with 19592 free, and could not complete a DHCP handshake with a phone sitting two feet away - a failure that looks like a broken web server and is not one. Any future board should be checked against the CYD's numbers, not against its own datasheet's headline.

RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT, and the answer is that both profiles are right. This board and the verified waveshare-s3-touch-lcd-147 carry the SAME 172x320 ST7789 panel at the same rotation and the same col_offset 34, and they disagree on two fields: this board wants invert true / mirror_x false, the S3 wants invert false / mirror_x true. Both were confirmed on their own glass. So the panel part number does NOT determine these two - how the module is wired and mounted does, and the vendor's own BSP is the better witness for a given board than a sibling board with the same LCD. The practical rule: never copy invert or mirror across boards on the strength of a matching controller, even when everything else about the panel matches. Check it on first light; it costs one look at the screen.

The panel is 172 columns of a 240-column ST7789 frame memory, so it needs a RAM offset or everything is shifted. 34 is (240-172)/2, the panel centred in the controller window. THIS USED TO BE THE BSP'S JOB and is now penguinOS's: with driver_source esp_lcd, eos_display_st7789.c makes the esp_lcd_panel_set_gap(34, 0) and esp_lcd_panel_invert_color(true) calls itself, from col_offset/row_offset and invert in this file. The symptom of dropping the gap is a picture that looks fine but is nudged sideways.

The microSD sits on the same SPI host as the panel: CLK GPIO7 and MOSI GPIO6 are shared, MISO GPIO5 and CS GPIO4 are the card's own. Every card access has to take the panel's bus lock, and card traffic during a flush will tear the frame.
The board has BOOT and RESET buttons but the BSP does not expose their GPIOs and nobody has traced them, so none are declared here. Confirm on hardware before binding a key to one.
MISO is not wired to the panel. Nothing can be read back from the controller, which also means no register read can ever identify it.
